messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High auth error-rate for customer 'OrionData' on VPC bridge (dedicated pool id: dp-orion-03). Error class: 401 / OIDC validation failures and mTLS handshake errors observed. Impact: customer-traffic degraded, some requests failing instantly. Paging on-call.

maria (oncall): ack. I'm pulling logs from the auth-bridge. @OrionOps can you confirm you rolled any certs/keys in the last hour?

OrionOps: Hey Maria, we rotated a tenant key at 09:12 UTC and rolled a new intermediate at 09:20 for our internal CA. Notified support but didn't touch Redwood side. We saw errors around 09:25.

maria (oncall): got it. looking at bridge logs now. seeing repeated: ``\"jwks fetch failed: kid not found\"`` plus TLS handshake errors: ``tls: certificate verify failed: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority``. Seems like two symptoms.

adeel: read the logs you pasted earlier — the jwks kid mismatch usually means the bridge cached a JWKS set with old kid and customer's OIDC issuer rotated keys before cache TTL expired. But the TLS verify error suggests our bridge isn't accepting their new intermediate CA for mTLS.

keisha: pinging infra team — did we change the keystore rotation policy? The bridge should be pulling tenant trust bundles from the VPC config every 30s.

tyler: checking config. The auth-bridge runs a local trust-bundle watcher that hits control-plane endpoint /v1/tenants/<id>/trustbundle. Last successful fetch for dp-orion-03 at 09:14, then 09:16, then gaps. I see a 503 from control-plane at 09:18 that coincides with their key rotation. That could explain stale JWKS cached locally.

samir: If control-plane returned 503, the bridge might have fallen back to the cached certs and not detected the intermediate change. For immediate mitigation we can force-refresh the trust bundle and JWKS cache on the bridge. Command to run on bridge (dp-orion-03):

```
# on auth-bridge host
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/internal/refresh-trust && curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/internal/refresh-jwks
systemctl restart auth-bridge
```

maria (oncall): before restarting, we should assess risk. Restart will drop in-flight connections for that customer's long-lived streams. OrionOps, do you have many long-lived sessions? Any background jobs that can't tolerate disconnects?

OrionOps: We have a few streaming ingestion agents (low-rate) that will reconnect; ok to restart as long as we coordinate. Please proceed.

maria (oncall): ok doing an in-place trigger first (no full restart). Running refresh endpoints now.

maria (oncall): ``curl.../internal/refresh-trust`` returned 200, but ``/internal/refresh-jwks`` still failing with 504 from control-plane. I'm going to temporarily enable a compatibility mode on the bridge that will accept the new client cert chain by ignoring intermediate validation for tenant dp-orion-03 and fall back to a soft-accept policy. This is risky but limits customer impact while we fix control-plane.

adeel: how do we toggle that? we have a runtime flag `--trusted-bundle-mode=soft-accept` per-tenant.

maria (oncall): flipping flag now on the pool router. Command:

```
rdctl pools update dp-orion-03 --set auth.bridge.trustMode=soft-accept
```

maria (oncall): flag applied. Immediate drop in TLS errors (logs show successful mutual auth from Orion agents). JWKS errors still present for token validation though (kid mismatch). I suspect their OIDC provider rotated keys and our cache hasn't been refreshed due to the control-plane 503.

keisha: can we route Orion traffic to our shared-compat pool temporarily (shared pool id: sp-compat-01) to keep traffic through a proxy that pulls JWKS directly from the issuer rather than the cached bridge? That will incur additional egress but reduce customer-visible failures.

samir: we can, but need to ensure tenant isolation rules hold — traffic to shared pool will not access dedicated disk mounts. Orion agreed to temporary routing? @OrionOps

OrionOps: temporary route is fine. Our ingesters will reconnect. We prefer throughput over perfect session continuity.

maria (oncall): initiating routing change: ``rdctl route update tenant-orion --dest-pool=sp-compat-01 --reason=\"auth bridge degraded, jwks rotation\"``

maria (oncall): routing change applied. Monitoring for errors... Errors dropping to near zero, successful token validations increasing.

adeel: good. Next step: fix control-plane 503. I see that the control-plane had a transient outage due to a mis-scheduled DB migration job that started at 09:17 and caused increased latencies on tenant config endpoints. The migration was rolled back at 09:31, but some caches didn't backfill.

keisha: I'm going to replay tenant config cache push for Orion on control-plane so bridges can pull fresh trust bundles. Command:

```
# control-plane admin
cpctl tenants push-config --tenant=orion --force
```

keisha: push-config returned ok at 09:46. Bridges started pulling new trust bundle at 09:47.

maria (oncall): now that JWKS and trust can refresh, I'm going to revert the compatibility flag and move Orion back to dedicated pool after observing stability for 5m.

samir: note: before moving back, we'll perform a token validation sweep to ensure no regression. Script:

```
python tools/sanity_check_tokens.py --tenant orion --jwks-url https://oidc.orion.internal/.well-known/jwks.json
```

maria (oncall): sweep passed. Reverting flag and routing now.

maria (oncall): ``rdctl pools update dp-orion-03 --set auth.bridge.trustMode=strict``

maria (oncall): routing back to dp-orion-03. Observing traffic... metrics stable for 10m. No further 401s or tls verify errors.

OrionOps: thanks team. We confirmed our agents re-authenticated and everything is green on our side.

maria (oncall): impact summary for postmortem: customer OrionData experienced ~14 minutes of elevated auth failures (09:25-09:39 window) due to control-plane 503 causing stale JWKS/trust bundle in auth-bridge after customer rotated keys. Mitigation steps: (1) soft-accept compatibility flag to reduce mTLS failures, (2) route to shared-compat pool to avoid cached JWKS, (3) forced config push from control-plane and refresh on bridges, (4) sanity token sweep, (5) revert to strict mode and route back. No other customers impacted; shared-compat pool had modest extra load but within limits.

maria (oncall): assigning postmortem owner to @adeel. Handoff to evening oncall @tyler — if anything regresses please alert.

tyler: ack, I'll keep an eye on dp-orion-03 for the next 6 hours.

adeel: will draft postmortem with timeline and follow-ups: add control-plane retry/backoff for tenant config endpoints, add immediate push capability when control-plane reports 5xx for a tenant, increase monitoring for JWKS TTL mismatch, and a small runbook to avoid toggling soft-accept without routing to shared pool.

maria (oncall): closing incident thread, marking resolved at 10:18 UTC. :white_check_mark:
